messages:
ashley: Heads-up — seeing nondeterministic eval failures during new-model bringup on staging. ~1/7 CI runs produce different completion tokens for the same seed and prompt.

miguel: Ugh. Any pattern? specific sampling params or quantization mode?

ashley: I think it correlates with: batched evals + top_p sampling + int8 kernels. Logs show same config but different outputs.

priya: Can you paste the runner config?

ashley: ```json
{
  \"seed\": null,
  \"batch_size\": 8,
  \"shuffle\": false,
  \"sampling\": {
    \"temperature\": 0.7,
    \"top_p\": 0.9
  },
  \"quantize\": \"bitsandbytes\"
}
```

miguel: seed:null — that's suspicious. If seed not set, different runs will be different obviously. But you said same seed + flake?

ashley: Right — in the failing CI runs we *do* pass SEED=12345 to the job env. The runner overrides it in a weird place. Here's the key loop snippet from eval-runner:```python
for worker in workers:
    seed = base_seed + worker.id
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    for batch in worker.batches():
        # call model.generate (uses internal RNG)
        out = model.generate(batch, sampling_args)
```

priya: That per-worker reseed pattern is deliberate to avoid identical streams across workers, but if worker ordering isn't deterministic between runs then the same example can be seen under different worker seeds. If the dataloader assignment to workers changes, outputs move around.

miguel: Exactly. On top of that, CUDA multinomial/torch.multinomial has historically been nondet across some CUDA/cuDNN combos when run in parallel. Also cudnn.benchmark=True can change algorithm selection.

ashley: CI image shows CUDA 11.8 + torch 2.1 and cudnn.benchmark default true in our runtime. I ran a quick local repro: with SEED=12345 and workers=4, two runs differed. Setting pthreads/worker pinning made them consistent.

taylor: Actionable fixes I see: 1) set a single process-level RNG seed at process start (not per-batch), 2) use explicit Generator objects passed into sampling ops, 3) disable cudnn.benchmark and enable deterministic algorithms during eval, 4) make worker->example assignment stable (stable hashing), 5) for nucleus sampling prefer a deterministic implementation (or use top_k for CI).

ashley: Proposed short-term patch: set runner config to: ```yaml
seed: 12345
shuffle: false
cudnn_benchmark: false
use_deterministic_algorithms: true
sampling: { temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.0 }
``` and add a CI job that runs the eval 5x and asserts identical outputs.

priya: That will mask sampling variability by forcing greedy (temp 0), but we want to test sampling determinism too. For sampling tests we should set explicit torch.Generator and use torch.multinomial with that generator on CPU or a deterministic CPU fallback. Example: ```py
gen = torch.Generator(device='cpu').manual_seed(seed)
probs = logits.softmax(-1)
idx = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1, generator=gen)
```

miguel: Also consider stateless sampling: use a keyed RNG per-sequence (e.g., siphash prompt+idx -> seed) so sampling doesn't depend on worker ordering. That decouples ordering from outputs.

ashley: Good call. I'll prototype stateless generator + stable assignment.

ci-bot: Test run queued: r=refs/heads/main eval-flake-matrix x5 (SEED=12345). Results will post here. :gear:

ops-bot: Note: we should avoid enabling full deterministic algos in prod inference (perf tradeoffs). Make CI-only flags.

ashley: Agreed — CI-only. Plan: priya takes deterministic sampling wrapper (stateless + generator), miguel stabilizes worker assignment and CI job, I will add the flaky-eval GH action. Target PR by EOD tomorrow.

taylor: Also add a regression test that runs the same prompt+seed across quantized kernels (FP16, int8) to catch kernel nondet. Small harness: run 3 kernels x 5 repeats and assert exact match or record per-token divergences.

priya: I'll add that test to eval-tests and mark as flaky-gated (only run in nightly if too slow).

miguel: If anyone hits CUDA nondet at sampling level, let's also try updating torch and CUDA drivers — there've been fixes for multinomial nondeterminism in patch releases.

ashley: Thanks all. Will open the PRs with diffs and CI matrix. Posting repro snippets & failing outputs in the PR comment. :white_check_mark:
